subject: Private offer: metered burst credits & dealer uplift mechanics
messages:

Cc: BrightBridge Sales <sales@brightbridge.io>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private offer: brief on burst credits and channel uplift ask

Jordan — thanks again for the call earlier. Two quick follow-ups from our finance and procurement teams at Clearwell: they want the private offer to include (1) a small pool of "burst credits" that don't count against committed usage but can be consumed in spikes, and (2) clarity on how BrightBridge (our reseller) will be compensated when those bursts are consumed.

Concrete asks: 
- Can Redwood provide a 10% pool of monthly committed tokens as non-billable burst credits for the first 6 months?
- If bursts exceed that pool, Clearwell wants overage to be billed at a predictable uplift (we suggested +15% to list).
- BrightBridge needs a guaranteed dealer uplift (commission) on all overage tokens that flow through marketplace billing — they asked for a 6% pass-through on overage revenue.

We understand there are technical nuances (metering/attribution and marketplace SKU mapping) — can you confirm feasible approaches and what documentation you need from our side to keep this in the private-offer and PO logic? Attaching the procurement brief.

Thanks,
Sophie Park
Head of Cloud Procurement
Clearwell Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private offer: brief on burst credits and channel uplift ask

Team — looping you on Clearwell's ask (see attached). High level: they want a token pool for burst capacity that doesn’t count against committed consumption, predictable overage pricing, and a reseller uplift for BrightBridge on overage.

Key constraints to consider:
- Marketplace private-offer wiring (AWS/GCP/Azure) typically maps committed SKUs to list-price buckets; non-billable burst credits can't be a native SKU — we surface them as credit adjustments in billing or via a periodic invoice credit.
- Overage attribution path: the marketplace will bill overage to Clearwell, but dealer uplift/commissioning needs to be triggered by the invoiced overage amount; some clouds support reseller pass-through fields, others require a reconciliation flow.

Options I see: 
A) Token-credit pool implemented as a monthly invoice credit line (our side creates a credit GL for the 10% pool). Pros: simple to implement and consistent across marketplaces. Cons: not visible in raw usage telemetry; reconciliation required for channel.

B) Create a separate metered SKU named CLEARW-BURST (zero-rate up to pool, then rate at uplift if consumed). Pros: easy attribution by SKU. Cons: requires marketplace SKU onboarding and buyer acceptance — takes longer.

C) Hybrid: internal usage tagging + monthly crediting to mirror pool consumption, with a separate overage SKU to capture excess for attribution.

Ask: Ben/Laura — can you validate projected ARR delta and commission cadence if we go with A vs B? Irene — what's the fastest path for a temporary marketplace SKU? I'm attaching my pricing calc (WIP) — fill in channel uplift math and return.

Thanks,
Jordan
Director, Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference

Jordan — quick read: ran the numbers on A vs B and sketched channel flows. Short answers and then details below.

Short answers: 
- We can support the 10% monthly burst pool as an invoice credit (Option A) with minimal engineering/marketplace lead time.
- To honor BrightBridge's 6% uplift on overage, we'll need a reconciliation workflow and a monthly pass-through payout (not all clouds provide native overage commission links).
- Option B (separate SKU) gives cleaner attribution and immediate commission triggers where the marketplace supports reseller pass-through, but SKU onboarding adds ~3-5 weeks for GCP/Azure and potentially longer for AWS private offers.

Numbers (example for Q1):
- Committed monthly tokens equivalent: 100M tokens at list $0.0008/token => $80,000 list/month.
- 10% burst pool value (non-billable) => $8,000/month credit applied.
- If bursts exceed pool by 20M tokens => overage at list * 1.15 => $18,400 overage. BrightBridge 6% on overage revenue => $1,104 payout.

Operational notes: 
1) If we implement A, we create a monthly invoice credit and a simple accounting tag so BrightBridge can receive a monthly statement for their uplift calculation — payout via partner ledger.
2) If we implement B, we ask Clearwell to accept a CLEARW-BURST SKU in the private offer; marketplace will bill it directly and reseller attribution is immediate where supported.

Recommendation: Start with Option A to meet procurement timelines; parallel-track SKU onboarding (Option B) for durable attribution. I can draft the reconciliation SOP and partner payout cadence.

Irene — please advise on the current ETA for temporary SKU creation in GCP and whether Azure can do it faster. Laura — can you draft an amendment to the private offer language that codifies the monthly credit & overage uplift?

Ben Carter
Sr. Director, Marketplace GTM
Redwood Inference
